At the heart of a bicycle’s gear-shifting system is the derailleur, a mechanical device that moves the chain laterally across a series of sprockets with varying sizes. When the rider manipulates the shifters mounted on the handlebars, they pull or release a specific amount of cable tension connected to the derailleur. This tension change causes the derailleur’s internal spring mechanism to move its cage either inward toward the bike’s frame or outward away from it, effectively pushing or pulling the chain to ensure it engages properly with the next gear size without skipping or jamming.
